take_homes: Two reusable checks, one on company policy and one on agent risk, packaged as a skill that I can give to my team so they don't each build their own.
Agent risk is mostly about what the agent can reach and what text it reads. Scoping access down beats patching afterwards.
Every mitigation leaves a residual risk, and I write it down and sign for it. 'I can't tell' is a legitimate row and needs evidence to close.

monday.move: Run the security skill on the usage-pricing pilot agents, pick one risk, apply one mitigation, and put the residual in the report for the pricing working group.
monday.who: me, then I share the skill with two of my fourteen
monday.stop_condition: one risk mitigated and a residual recorded; anything unclear goes to legal as a narrow question
monday.blocker: We have no shared place for the skill and context files, so I'd have to send it round by hand.

misconception.why: The useful output was a packaged method with reports and rules in a file, and no prompt did that work. I still think wording matters, but it isn't what makes a team's use of agents good.

one_line: Good hands-on hours where I built a security check my team can reuse, but the lecture repeats itself and the homework is about other people's cases.
